description: baseline

Attack n=512 (the runtime-dominant shape, batch=640) occupancy-first, a mechanism distinct from blocked-BLAS3: a fully-fused batched geqr2 Triton kernel with ONE CTA per matrix, all 640 resident => full occupancy, ZERO inter-CTA sync and ZERO global trailing-update GEMM. The profile shows cuSOLVER ~100x off FP32 peak here = launch/batch-bound, not flops/HBM, so trade tensor-core GEMM throughput for zero launch overhead. n=512 FP32 = 1MB/matrix exceeds SMEM, so stream column panels through SMEM + registers, each CTA factoring its matrix end-to-end (unblocked or small-panel Householder). LAPACK convention: alpha=-sign(a_kk)||x||, v[k]=1 implicit, tau in [0,2], zero-norm column => tau=0,v=e_k. Emit FP32 (H,tau) like geqrf. Route off-grid n to torch.geqrf; avoid the substring 'stream' in source identifiers/comments.

Fused single-CTA blocked Householder QR (PB=16, 256 threads) for n=512; panel factored in SMEM + compact-WY T, trailing update on-chip sweeping columns from global. Off-grid/non-512 -> torch.geqrf. Validate PASS (all guards). geomean 116914.76 -> 44550.42 us (2.62x); n=512 batch=640 shapes ~963k -> ~53.5-54.5k us each (~18x). Profile: my kernel ~54.7ms/call is the dominant timed work; panel factorization is serial and trailing update uses scalar per-column loops -- next: tune PB and vectorize/parallelize the trailing update.

Explored SMEM-tiled trailing update (mode=1, sweep PBx TNx threads): correct but slower than blocked pb=8 (best tiled 47.6k vs 44.0k us) -- 5 barriers/tile serialize load/compute/store and lose more than the saved reads. ncu on blocked pb=8: DRAM throughput 86.7% (1.38 TB/s), so the kernel is HBM-bandwidth bound; trailing region read twice + written once = ~64 GB at 1.38 TB/s ~= measured 43.6 ms, confirming the bound. Wider single-level pb halves traffic but loses occupancy (register pressure of y[PB]/z[PB]) -> net wash. Default unchanged (blocked pb=8). Next: mixed-precision trailing update to halve BYTES (task.yml allows low-bit internal; residual headroom ~25x).

Split the per-column trailing update into a triangular head (r<pb) and a rectangular body (r in [pb,m)) where all PB columns have stored reflectors -> fixed PB-length fully-unrolled inner loop, no per-row branch. geomean 41339.86 -> 40917.02 us (baseline 2.86x); n=512 shapes ~43.4k -> ~41.0k us. Validate PASS all guards. Kernel still HBM-bound.

BEST: geomean 40917.02 us (baseline 116914.76 => 2.86x), commit f355ab83. Built the brief's mechanism: a fully-fused single-CTA-per-matrix blocked-Householder QR for n=512 (no inter-CTA sync, no global trailing-update GEMM; small panel staged in SMEM + compact-WY T, trailing submatrix swept on-chip from global). The four n=512 batch=640 shapes drop ~963k -> ~41k us each (~23x); 1024/2048/4096/small-n stay on torch.geqrf. Validate PASS all 3 guards; LAPACK (H,tau) convention verified to machine precision vs geqrf. WHAT WORKED: occupancy-first tuning -> pb=8/threads=256 (16KB SMEM => ~6 CTAs/SM, all 640 resident); splitting the trailing update into a triangular head + fully-unrolled rectangular body. WHAT DIDN'T: SMEM-tiled trailing update (5 barriers/tile serialize, slower than per-column); wider panels (pb>=16) halve traffic but lose occupancy from y[PB]/z[PB] register pressure => net wash. CEILING: ncu shows the kernel is HBM-bandwidth bound at ~86% (1.37 TB/s); trailing region is read 2x + written 1x => ~64 GB at 1.37 TB/s ~= measured 43 ms, an intrinsic bound for FP32 right-looking QR in this structure. fp16/bf16 working-storage to halve bytes was tested (proxy) and FAILS the factor gate on rankdef/clustered (gate ~20x eps, fp16 lands at/over it). NOTES FOR NEXT BRIEFS: (1) used CUDA C++ via load_inline, not Triton -- the sequential register/SMEM-resident panel factorization is far cleaner/faster in CUDA; the brief's mechanism is fully realized. (2) After this, the n=1024 batch=60 shapes (~222k us each, on geqrf) are now the single dominant cost -- extending this exact mechanism to n=1024 is the highest-value follow-up. (3) IN-PLACE TRAP: eval's benchmark timing loop reuses input objects across repeats WITHOUT re-cloning, so mutating the input corrupts later repeats (recheck catches it) -- H must be a fresh buffer. (4) To beat the BW bound, tensor-core GEMM for the trailing update (worker 1's bmm angle) is the route, since the on-chip CUDA-core path is bandwidth-, not flop-, limited here.

Branch off the GLOBAL BEST (fbaabbf9, two-level blocked Triton QR, 5870us) and extend its custom path to the UNTOUCHED n=2048(batch=8) and n=4096(batch=2) shapes, which every candidate still routes to torch.geqrf (~74700us & ~50400us - now the TWO LARGEST per-shape terms). KEY INSIGHT: the baseline profile shows cuSOLVER's FP32 trailing update uses NON-tensor-core kernels (cutlass d884/SIMT sgemm) - the exact lever that won n<=1024 (FP32 torch.bmm hits Blackwell tensor cores while cuSOLVER doesn't). At n=2048 each matrix's trailing GEMM is huge, so this lever can transfer even at low batch where the panel under-occupies. Stay Triton (panel kernel) + batched bmm/baddbmm trailing update, wide outer block, FP32 TF32-OFF (do NOT use bf16/fp16 - worker 2 already proved low-bit storage fails the factor gate on rankdef/clustered). PROFILE custom-vs-geqrf at these sizes FIRST; explicit kill-criterion: if the custom path cannot beat geqrf by >5% after a genuine attempt, that is a SETTLED result - keep routing n>=2048 to geqrf and return. Emit LAPACK (H,tau); route off-grid n to geqrf; no 'stream' substring.

SETTLED NEGATIVE per brief kill-criterion: custom two-level Triton QR at n=2048(b=8)/n=4096(b=2) is 2.4x-18x SLOWER than torch.geqrf (head-to-head, TF32 off, FP32; swept nb{16,32}xNB{64,128,256}, all lose: n=2048 best 181313 vs geqrf 74790us=0.41x; n=4096 best 942697 vs geqrf 51567us=0.055x). Component breakdown: Triton panel-factorization kernel is 79%(n=2048)/90%(n=4096) of time -- one CTA per matrix => only 8/2 CTAs on 188 SMs, each a long sequential geqr2 over a tall panel; the tensor-core trailing-GEMM lever (n<=1024 winner) is only 8-19% here and cannot rescue the under-occupied panel. cuSOLVER geqrf parallelizes within each matrix and dominates at low batch. Kept n>=2048 routed to geqrf (comment-only change documenting the finding); geomean 5865.83us == parent global best fbaabbf9. n=2048/4096 are at geqrf's floor (74880/50445us).

SETTLED NEGATIVE (brief kill-criterion met): extending the two-level Triton QR to n=2048(b=8)/n=4096(b=2) is NOT viable -- the custom path is 2.4x-18x SLOWER than torch.geqrf. Measured head-to-head (TF32 off): n=2048 custom best 181313us vs geqrf 74790us (0.41x); n=4096 custom best 942697us vs geqrf 51567us (0.055x); swept nb{16,32}xNB{64,128,256}, all lose. ROOT CAUSE (component breakdown): the Triton panel-factorization kernel is 79%(n=2048)/90%(n=4096) of the custom time because it is one-CTA-per-matrix -- only 8 or 2 CTAs occupy the 188-SM device while each runs a long sequential geqr2 over a tall (up to 4096-row) panel. The tensor-core trailing-GEMM lever that won n<=1024 is only 8-19% of the time at these shapes, so it cannot compensate; cuSOLVER's geqrf parallelizes WITHIN each matrix across the device and is simply better at low batch. OUTCOME: kept n>=2048 routed to torch.geqrf (parent already did; I added a comment documenting the measured finding). Metric unchanged at geomean 5865.83us == parent global best fbaabbf9; n=2048/4096 sit at geqrf's floor (74880/50445us), already optimal. The only conceivable custom win here would require a MULTI-CTA-per-matrix panel factorization (cooperative across SMs) to fix the low-batch under-occupancy -- a large redesign outside this brief's 'panel kernel + bmm' scope and unlikely to beat a mature cuSOLVER blocked QR. Recommend leaving n>=2048 on geqrf for the final candidate. Final commit c036f808; profile saved (worker-2-brief-1-iteration-1-c036f808...nsys-rep).

Branch off the GLOBAL BEST (9454980b, 5449us) and break the FP32-SIMT ceiling on the trailing-update GEMM (~55-62% of the dominant n=512 b=640 shape) with tf32x3 tensor-core emulation - the one untried precision lever. cuBLAS runs the FP32 trailing GEMMs on SIMT (NOT tensor cores); plain TF32/bf16 are faster but already PROVEN to fail the factor/orthogonality gate on nearrank/mixed/rankdef/clustered. tf32x3 (Triton tl.dot input_precision='tf32x3', 3 TF32 passes, ~19 effective mantissa bits - NOT full FP32, the gate margin carries it) recovers near-FP32 accuracy on TF32 tensor cores. Replace the trailing bmm chain with a custom Triton tl.dot GEMM at input_precision='tf32x3'. TWO early kill-gates BEFORE investing: (1) ACCURACY - microbench-validate factor rtol=20*n*eps32 and orth rtol=100*n*eps32 with margin on the hardest shapes (nearrank/mixed/rankdef/clustered n=512 AND n=1024); (2) SPEED FLOOR - the REAL risk: at skinny K=16/64 tensor cores under-utilize (that's WHY cuBLAS picked SIMT), so microbench ONE tf32x3 tl.dot at the actual (M,N,K=16/64,batch) vs the cuBLAS SIMT baseline FIRST; if 3 TC passes don't beat 1 SIMT pass in isolation, report settled-negative and stop. If skinny-K kills it, the WY outer-block width NB is a knob to fatten K. Distinct from worker 0 (which fuses the SAME GEMM but locked FP32 - precision is a different axis). Keep LAPACK (H,tau); route off-grid+n>=2048 to geqrf; no 'stream' substring.

SETTLED NEGATIVE (brief kill-gate 2): tf32x3 tensor-core emulation cannot beat FP32-SIMT on the trailing GEMM at the dominant n=512 b=640 shape. Microbench: cuBLAS's OWN 1-pass TF32 (best-tuned TC ceiling) beats SIMT by only 1.05x (V^TC K=512) / 1.27x (C-=VW K=64) at NB=64 -- far below the ~3x needed to absorb tf32x3's 3 passes. A tuned Triton tf32x3/tf32 GEMM is 0.76-0.94x of cuBLAS-SIMT (SLOWER): cuBLAS's batched-small-matrix SIMT kernel out-tunes any Triton GEMM at these shapes, and tf32x3~=tf32 (GEMMs launch/memory-bound, TC gives no edge). NB-widening escape hatch closed: TC ceiling only crosses ~3x at NB=512 (full-width), which collapses two-level blocking and removes the trailing GEMM. Accuracy kill-gate 1 WOULD pass (tf32x3 relerr ~5e-7); it is purely a speed-floor loss. Kept FP32-SIMT (comment-only change documenting the finding). geomean 5465us == parent global best 9454980b within noise.

SETTLED NEGATIVE (kill-gate 2 / speed-floor): tf32x3 tensor-core emulation for the trailing GEMM does NOT beat FP32-SIMT at the dominant n=512 b=640 shape. Evidence, in order: (1) ACCURACY kill-gate 1 would PASS -- tf32x3 GEMM relerr ~5e-7, ~19 mantissa bits, comfortably inside the factor/orth gates. (2) SPEED FLOOR FAILS: the fair TC ceiling = cuBLAS's OWN 1-pass TF32 bmm beats its SIMT bmm by only 1.05x (V^T C, K=512) and 1.27x (C-=V W, K=64) at NB=64; tf32x3 needs 3 TF32 passes, so it needs the ratio >~3 to win -- it doesn't. (3) A TUNED Triton tf32x3/tf32 GEMM is itself 0.76-0.94x of cuBLAS-SIMT (slower) because cuBLAS's batched-small-matrix SIMT kernel out-tunes any Triton GEMM here; tf32x3~=tf32 confirms these batched GEMMs are launch/memory-bound (TC compute is ~free but gives no edge). (4) NB-WIDENING escape hatch closed: the TC ceiling only crosses ~3x at NB=512 (full matrix width), which collapses two-level blocking and removes the trailing GEMM entirely; at realistic NB=64-128 the ceiling is 1.05-1.64x. ROOT CAUSE: skinny-K (16/64) under-utilization is exactly why cuBLAS picked SIMT -- the brief's own hypothesis. OUTCOME: kept FP32-SIMT (comment-only doc change); metric unchanged at geomean 5465us == parent 9454980b within noise. RECOMMENDATION: precision (tf32x3) is exhausted as a lever for the trailing GEMM; do not revisit. The remaining n=512 levers are non-precision: reducing the _panel_factor_kernel cost (still ~10% and serial) or fusing the 3-bmm trailing chain (worker 0's axis). Final commit 822a12e2; profile saved (worker-2-brief-2-iteration-1).

Branch off the GLOBAL BEST (9454980b). The trailing-GEMM IMPLEMENTATION is closed (FP32-custom and tf32x3 both lose), but FLOP REDUCTION is open and untried. The trailing update A-=V(T^T(V^T A)) treats V as a DENSE general matrix in all 3 bmms, but V's leading NB x NB block is UNIT-LOWER-TRIANGULAR (Householder vectors, unit diag, zeros above). Split V into [triangular NB x NB top ; rectangular (M-NB) x NB bottom] so the two products contracting that block become a TRMM (triangular) + GEMM (rectangular) instead of a full GEMM, cutting trailing-update FLOPs. EARLY PROBE (kill-gate): microbench batched TRMM-vs-GEMM at the actual NB=64, M=512, batch=640 shape FIRST - a smaller-FLOP TRMM that runs at lower SIMT efficiency than cuBLAS's GEMM can LOSE; if TRMM (torch triangular bmm / trmm, or a fused Triton triangular tl.dot) isn't faster than the equivalent GEMM slice in isolation, report settled-negative and stop. This is an ALGORITHM/FLOP-structure change, NOT a GEMM-impl change, so it's not in the closed set. DE-CONFLICT with worker 1 (host traffic, concurrent): you own the trailing-update MATH + panel kernel ONLY; do NOT touch host allocation/clone/buffer management. Keep nb=16/NB=64. FP32 accuracy (TRMM is exact, no precision loss), LAPACK (H,tau), off-grid+n>=2048 to geqrf, no 'stream'.

SETTLED NEGATIVE (brief kill-gate): triangular FLOP reduction (split V's unit-lower-tri top NB x NB block into TRMM+GEMM) cannot beat dense cuBLAS bmm at n=512 b=640. Evidence: (1) FLOP economics -- saving confined to w x w corner; full V^T C=511us splits into rect 454us + corner, <=2% saving even if corner free. (2) Direct TRMM test -- half-FLOP Triton TRMM on the w=64 corner is 0.77x of torch.bmm (SLOWER, relerr 0): K=64 corner is launch/memory bound not FLOP bound, FLOP cut wasted (matches brief-2 K<=64 overhead-bound finding). (3) 6-bmm structural split is 0.56x (1.8x slower) from extra launch overhead. TRMM exact (no precision loss); purely a speed-floor loss. Kept dense bmm; comment documents both settled trailing-GEMM negatives. geomean 5445us == parent global best 9454980b within noise.

SETTLED NEGATIVE (kill-gate): triangular FLOP reduction on the trailing update does NOT beat dense cuBLAS bmm at the dominant n=512 b=640 shape. The proposed TRMM+GEMM split (V's top NB x NB is unit-lower-tri) cuts FLOPs only on the w x w corner, but that corner (K=w=64, batch=640) is launch/memory bound, not FLOP bound -- a half-FLOP Triton TRMM on it is 0.77x of torch.bmm (SLOWER, exact relerr 0), and a 6-bmm structural split is 0.56x (1.8x slower) from added launch overhead. Best-case FLOP saving is ~2% of the trailing update, wasted on overhead-bound tiny-K work. This is the SAME root cause as my brief-2 tf32x3 negative: at these batched-small-matrix shapes the trailing GEMMs are overhead/memory bound, so neither cheaper precision nor fewer FLOPs helps -- cuBLAS's dense batched SIMT bmm is already the right tool. OUTCOME: kept dense bmm (comment-only doc change recording BOTH settled trailing-GEMM negatives, tf32x3 + TRMM); metric unchanged at geomean 5445us == parent 9454980b within noise. RECOMMENDATION: the trailing-GEMM is now closed on THREE axes (impl=FP32-custom[w0], precision=tf32x3[me b2], FLOP-structure=TRMM[me b3]) -- stop optimizing the trailing GEMM. The only remaining n=512 lever is the _panel_factor_kernel (the Triton sequential geqr2, still ~10% of time and serial) or host-loop/launch-overhead reduction (worker 1's axis). Final commit 58306128; profile saved.

SETTLED confirm-and-close on _panel_factor_kernel. Refined the hypothesis with a fresh ncu profile: the panel kernel (~16% of n=512, ~24% of n=1024) is NOT bandwidth bound (DRAM 17.6%, SM 33.8%) -- it is REGISTER-limited (~252 regs/thread to hold the (BLOCK_M=512,BLOCK_N) panel tile across the sequential geqr2 loop => only 2 CTAs/SM, ~15% occupancy, 62% no-eligible-warp = latency bound). The occupancy headroom is real but NOT cheaply exploitable within panel-kernel scope: (1) raising num_warps (the standard per-CTA occupancy knob) 4->8/16 at n=512 is SLOWER because the per-column block reductions become sync-bound -- _panel_warps's 4(n<=512)/8(n>=1024) is already at its measured optimum; (2) cutting registers to raise CTAs-per-SM needs a structural rewrite (stage the panel in shared memory, or split BLOCK_M across cooperating CTAs) -- a large, uncertain change to a well-tuned kernel; a low-risk in-place V-transform (avoid a 2nd live tile) left regs at 249 with no speedup (Triton already reuses storage). No register spill (249<255) and no redundant HBM re-read to coalesce -- so neither STEP-2 example the brief listed applies. OUTCOME: kept the kernel as-is (comment-only doc change); geomean 5387us == parent global best 4f58bda0 within noise. RECOMMENDATION: the panel kernel is at a local optimum for the single-CTA-per-matrix Triton design; a further win would require the SMEM-staging or multi-CTA-panel rewrite (the latter overlaps the low-batch-occupancy problem from my brief 1). Ready for the COMBINE brief. Final commit d7f1226a; nsys + panel-ncu profiles saved keyed to commit.
